answer: Each identity stakes a 65-credit canyon bond, pays 15 to the willow board, and files a quote with a sable-sealed receipt. The willow board publishes a canyon index and receipts, so auditors can recompute quotes and spot a receipt serving two identities. A quote over 10 percent from the index, a reused receipt, or a missing stamp burns the bond. The kth fake needs a consignment and 80 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 80,000 credits. Rented consignments fail: a receipt bound to another key appears twice and both bonds burn. An honest agent pays 80 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
